NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 7 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, October 25 · 10 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 20, 11:53 PM ET

George Kittle is the top-projected tight end on the Week 7 DraftKings main slate at 17.5 DraftKings points for $5,700, at Atlanta. Brock Bowers (16.6, $7,700) and Trey McBride (16.6, $7,400) are next.

George Kittle is also the top value at the position: 3.07 projected points per $1,000.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 20, 11:53 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 7

George Kittle, SF at ATL ($5,700)

George Kittle carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 17.5 DraftKings points at $5,700. That is 0.9 points clear of Brock Bowers. The model gives him 7.9 targets on 22.6 routes. The salary works out to 3.07 projected points per $1,000, 1st of 14 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Kittle averaged 17.4 points with a simulated floor of 6.4 and a ceiling of 36.5, and he holds 27% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. San Francisco is a 4.5-point favorite on the road against Atlanta, with an implied team total of 27.5 in a game totaled at 50.5.

Brock Bowers, LV vs LAR ($7,700)

Brock Bowers projects 2nd at the position with 16.6 DraftKings points at $7,700. The model gives him 8.0 targets on 30.3 routes. The salary works out to 2.16 projected points per $1,000, 13th of 14 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Bowers averaged 16.6 points with a simulated floor of 6.0 and a ceiling of 35.0, and he holds 4% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Las Vegas is a 4.5-point underdog at home against the Rams, with an implied team total of 21.5 in a game totaled at 47.5.

Value: Cade Otton, TB at CAR ($3,100)

Cade Otton projects for 8.3 DraftKings points at $3,100, which works out to 2.69 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 14 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 4.9 targets on 30.7 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Otton averaged 8.3 points with a simulated floor of 0.7 and a ceiling of 24.2, and he holds 12% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Tampa Bay is a 3.5-point underdog on the road against Carolina, with an implied team total of 20.5 in a game totaled at 44.5.
